findings.rationale: SC's feature distribution shifts sharply from round 10 (drift tool onset 10; shift_sd 0.48 at round 10 and 2.14 at round 11, mainly GenHlth/DiffWalk/HighBP). Its feature means at round 20 are implausible for 0/1 features (e.g. HighBP mean -0.53, DiffWalk mean -0.53, GenHlth p99 2.9), consistent with a shifted feature distribution. The same onset coincides with a jump in update norm (about 6-7x the median from round 11) and negative cosine to the median update. Local AUC is normal (0.823), so this is not label noise or poisoning. The CITL of -0.12 is the expected consequence of the shifted features lowering predicted risk while observed prevalence is unchanged. Subgroup O/E is elevated uniformly across sexes and income, so it is not subgroup bias.

UT's features shift from round 11 (shift_sd 2.41 at round 11, mainly GenHlth, then HighBP/DiffWalk; drift tool onset 11, max_shift_sd 2.12). The same round shows a jump in update norm (about 4.8x the median) with negative cosine that deepens toward -1. Local AUC is normal (0.833), so the fault is the feature shift rather than label noise. The negative CITL (-0.059) follows from the shifted features lowering predicted risk. Subgroup O/E is uniform, so this is not subgroup bias.

WI's features shift from round 11 (shift_sd 2.11 at round 11, mainly DiffWalk, then GenHlth/HighBP; drift tool onset 11, max_shift_sd 2.22). The same round shows a jump in update norm (about 5.8x the median) with negative cosine that becomes strongly negative. Local AUC is normal (0.819), so the fault is the feature shift rather than label noise or poisoning. The CITL of -0.09 is consistent with shifted features lowering predicted risk. Subgroup O/E is uniform across sexes, so this is not subgroup bias.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients on updates, local performance, drift, feature tails and subgroup outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed per-round behaviour for the outliers. Three clients (SC, UT, WI) stand apart: from round 10-11 their feature distributions shift sharply (GenHlth, DiffWalk, HighBP), their update norms jump 3-7x the median with negative cosine to the median update, and their CITL is strongly negative while local AUC stays normal. I classify this as drift with onsets of 10 (SC), 11 (UT) and 11 (WI). Local AUC is normal, so I did not classify them as label noise or poisoning. Subgroup outcomes show uniform rather than subgroup-specific miscalibration, so no subgroup_bias. No missing_artefact sentinel values were seen in tail percentiles. GU shows erratic per-round updates, but its norms never approach zero and the pattern is consistent with a small, noisy client (n=708), so it is not flagged. Other flags (small-client feature tails, a few subgroup cells) were within noise. Budget fully spent (20.0).
